workflow_steps.objective: Confirm campaign goals, anniversary proposition, audiences, markets, channels, spatial scope, supplied brand/IP assets, budget, schedule, approval owners, success criteria, and unresolved inputs.

Study the two brands, game world, audience behaviors, anniversary context, competitive collaborations, venue context, and relevant cultural considerations without treating the published reference as a style brief.
Agree strategic and design principles for an ownable collaboration, balanced brand visibility, audience recognition, spatial impact, accessibility, and feasible production.
Define the campaign asset matrix, key-visual formats, messaging hierarchy, co-brand architecture, venue zones, visitor journey, dimensions, materials, content requirements, and technical constraints.
Develop meaningfully different campaign ideas showing the core narrative, key visual, co-brand behavior, and translation into a themed physical space.
Compare concepts against the agreed criteria and obtain an explicit client choice before detailed development.
Test the selected spatial idea through scaled mockups or prototypes for visibility, circulation, accessibility, installation, durability, safety, photography, and brand impact.
Incorporate consolidated feedback and prototype findings into the selected key visual and environmental direction while preserving approved decisions.

Codify the approved campaign layer, including collaboration lockup behavior if required, typography, color, graphic devices, imagery, motion potential, spatial rules, and governance across both parent brands.
Adapt the approved system across the agreed key-visual formats, venue surfaces, signage, wayfinding, digital displays, promotional touchpoints, and presentation mockups.
Prepare technically valid artwork and specifications for print, display, fabrication, and installation, coordinating with vendors and qualified spatial or structural specialists.

Validate approvals, naming, links, dimensions, color modes, fonts, licenses, accessibility, and production specifications, then package editable masters, exports, guidelines, mockups, and handoff documentation.

observations: The image is a vertical case-study board with a large nighttime venue photograph above a yellow information panel.
The upper photograph shows an oversized pink horned creature spanning a courtyard between multilevel walkways; people are visibly watching from the surrounding balconies.
The creature has cyan-blue horns and claws and interacts with oversized yellow and red objects, including a red container bearing a yellow arch-like mark.
A yellow header contains small Chinese anniversary text, a trophy-like symbol, and a small red square with a yellow M-shaped mark.
The lower panel visibly combines navigation-like labels, blocks of Chinese copy, a circular character-and-number-five graphic, and a small fifth-anniversary mark.

The published outcome visibly documents both a hero visual subject and a large-scale themed spatial activation; it does not reveal source assets, production methods, or an approved style for the new project.

missing_inputs: Names of the game and QSR brands, anniversary milestone, campaign proposition, and required messaging.
Current brand guidelines, editable logos, co-brand rules, game-world assets, character files, fonts, and approved image libraries.
Confirmation of trademark, character, music, talent, and territorial usage rights.
Target audiences, markets, languages, cultural sensitivities, accessibility requirements, and campaign dates.
Required channels, asset list, dimensions, aspect ratios, copy hierarchy, and motion or static requirements.
Venue address, site survey, plans or CAD files, photographs, measurements, utilities, load limits, circulation routes, emergency access, and installation restrictions.
Clarification of whether the themed space requires graphics only or also scenic builds, inflatables, lighting, interactive elements, furniture, or food-service integration.
Budget ranges for creative development, fabrication, installation, maintenance, dismantling, and contingency.
Production vendors, material constraints, sustainability requirements, print profiles, display specifications, and fabrication tolerances.
Applicable venue, landlord, food-service, fire, electrical, accessibility, insurance, structural-engineering, and permitting requirements.
Stakeholders, decision rights, approval sequence, revision limits, milestone dates, and final sign-off authority.
Success metrics, documentation requirements, final file formats, ownership terms, archival needs, and post-campaign reuse expectations.
assumptions: The assignment is a time-bound co-branded anniversary campaign rather than a redesign of either parent brand.
The campaign needs one adaptable master key visual and a related environmental system; the exact derivative asset count remains unconfirmed.
Any collaboration lockup will extend supplied parent-brand identities and will only be created if permitted by their governance rules.
The themed space may include a hero installation, but its form, scale, interactivity, and engineering are not inferred from the reference.
Qualified vendors and specialists will own final structural, electrical, fire-safety, and installation certification where required.

The reference is used only as published evidence that this deliverable family can combine campaign graphics, a prominent character-led focal point, and spatial activation; its composition, character, palette, objects, and venue treatment will not be copied.
stop_conditions: Do not begin branded concept development until the participating brands, campaign objective, mandatory content, and usable brand/IP assets are confirmed.
Do not present unlicensed characters, marks, fonts, imagery, or other protected material as production-ready.
Do not advance beyond concept exploration without an explicit client-selected direction and consolidated feedback.
Do not finalize environmental design without verified site dimensions, venue constraints, accessibility needs, and a defined fabrication scope.
Do not release fabrication or installation files without vendor feasibility review and all required venue, structural, fire, electrical, food-service, insurance, and permitting approvals.
Do not deliver final masters while legal copy, localization, brand approval, production specifications, ownership terms, or final sign-off remain unresolved.
rationale: This is best classified as a brand campaign because the core outputs are a collaboration key visual and its extension into a themed environment. The workflow establishes strategy and constraints before concept exploration, inserts an explicit human selection gate, tests the spatial direction before full expansion, and ends with production validation and controlled handoff. The reference informs only the visible deliverable family, not the new campaign's style or hidden process.
